messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming_latency_slo_breach detected in shared-gpu-pool-3. p95 480ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.1s -> 6.8s over last 5m. Streaming stalls and client backpressure observed. Paging oncall: ashley.
ashley (oncall): on it. seeing alert in console. any service ownership notes? which tenant(s) look dominant?
miguel (sre): looks like a single tenant (tenant: flowly-prod) is high-IO on /dev/nvme1n1, causing cgroup writeback thrash. node-gpu-17 shows iowait spike and GPU stalls. attaching quick logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:21:30Z] node-gpu-17 iowait=42% r+w=720MB/s
[2026-03-15T10:22:01Z] kubelet cgroup writeback rate-limit hit: 1048576 bytes/s
[2026-03-15T10:22:05Z] inference-runtime: stalled streamer=flowly/stream-123 seq=4321
```
ashley (oncall): noted. severity? customer-facing?
miguel (sre): severity=high. Flowly has several active streaming sessions; product reports stalled frames and reconnects. p99 spike correlates with a large long-running batch job they started ~10:20.
sam (eng-runtime): can we throttle at runtime (per-tenant token-bucket) or fallback to smaller model? We have hot-path that can downgrade to a CPU-safe path for streaming but high latencies will persist if IO limited.
viktor (infra): prepping node-level mitigations: increasing blkio throttle for flowly cgroup, and prepping live-evac to move pods to dedicated-gpu-pool-2. but eviction will drop in-flight streams.
jess (product): customer impact: Flowly's SLAs are 99.9% streaming continuity. Ops: please prioritize minimizing disconnects, call flowly success contact?
ashley (oncall): decision time. We need immediate mitigation to stop p99 from spiking while avoiding mass disconnects. Options: 1) soft throttle tenant IO (throttle writeback), 2) migrate tenant pods to dedicated pool (short disconnects), 3) disable batching for tenant to reduce IO. Thoughts?
miguel (sre): go with hybrid: 1) apply soft blkio throttle to cap background writes, 2) flip runtime per-tenant batching->single-stream mode (lowers throughput but reduces write bursts), 3) if p99 still > 2s after 90s, initiate live-evac to dedicated pool. I'll run commands now.
ashley (oncall): do it. coordinate with infra. notify customer.
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: apply blkio cgroup throttle (throttle.bps_device) -> command:
```
echo "8:1 52428800" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/flowly.slice/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```
miguel (sre): applying throttle on node-gpu-17...
(brief pause)
miguel (sre): throttle applied. switching runtime config for tenant flowly -> batching=off, max_concurrency=2 via API: `POST /internal/tenants/flowly/config {"batching":false,"concurrency":2}`
sam (eng-runtime): runtime change accepted, streams set to single-frame flush. starting to see decreased write bursts in metrics. p95 improving.
(5m later)
miguel (sre): p95 down to 420ms, p99 = 1.8s. still above target but trending down. IO on node decreased ~60%.
viktor (infra): we still have elevated GPU queue in node-gpu-17. recommending live-evac now to be safe; will drain pods to dedicated-gpu-pool-2 with minimal disruption using graceful stream handoff. kicking evac job.
ashley (oncall): execute evac. coordinate with eng-runtime to honor streaming handoff TTL. notify customer.
sam (eng-runtime): initiating graceful handoff: `POST /internal/evac?tenant=flowly&target_pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-2&grace=30s`
miguel (sre): starting pod migration. monitoring reconnects.
(transition logs)
```
[2026-03-15T10:33:12Z] pod/flowly-stream-abc draining connections
[2026-03-15T10:33:20Z] handoff: new pod/flowly-stream-def accepted on dedicated-gpu-pool-2
[2026-03-15T10:33:41Z] connection switched, stream resumed
```
jess (product): got a msg from Flowly support: they saw a brief glitch ~10:33, then streams recovered. want a follow-up email.
ashley (oncall): customer impact summary for pager: Flowly experienced ~2-4s stalls for some streams during 10:20-10:34. No sustained disconnects after mitigation; sessions resumed. Risk: if tenant runs same batch job it'll repeat.
miguel (sre): promoting short-term mitigations -> long-term actions: 1) require tenant-level IO caps on shared pools, 2) auto-evac thresholds when cgroup writeback > X for >Y seconds, 3) improve runtime backpressure to shed batch jobs earlier.
viktor (infra): infra follow-ups: tune cgroup writeback limits, add node-level iops alerts, and preemptive eviction windows when GPU queue > Z.
sam (eng-runtime): runtime follow-ups: add streaming-safe downgrade path that avoids heavy disk writeback (in-memory kv cache bump), and make per-tenant batching default configurable via console.
jess (product): I'll own customer comms and coordinate credits if needed.
ashley (oncall): creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem. tags: multi-tenant-io, streaming-slo, noisy-tenant.
ops-runbook-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-4207 assigned to miguel. postmortem owner: ashley.
miguel (sre): adding timeline + logs to incident. will run blameless postmortem.
ashley (oncall): thanks team. will follow up in #incidents with incident doc and customer note draft. :thumbsup:
(threads continues with minor follow-ups but no more paging)
